newsitem.title: GRENADA: Grenada prime minister plans Cuba visit this month.
newsitem.headline: Grenada prime minister plans Cuba visit this month.

text.p: Grenada Prime Minister Keith Mitchell said on Tuesday he would visit Cuba later this month, a trip that would make him the first leader of his country to visit Cuba since the United States invaded Grenada in 1983.

The Caribbean News Agency reported that Mitchell planned a four-day visit beginning on April 21. In Cuba, he planned to seek assistance in construction of a national stadium in Grenada, as well as health care scholarships for Grenadian students.
Sports Minister Adrian Mitchell also was to form part of the 13-member delegation visiting Cuba.

Mitchell's New National Party has been seeking to improve relations with Cuba since it took office two years ago. The last Grenadian leader to visit Cuba was Prime Minister Maurice Bishop of the People's Revolutionary Government, whose murder helped spark the U.S. invasion of the island.

Bishop was deposed after a power struggle within his government in 1983, after which he and many of his followers were murdered by a rival faction. The chaos that followed prompted the U.S. invasion, which in turn was followed by the expulsion of Cubans who had been engaged in building a new airport and other projects on Grenada.

Mitchell's visit also would mark the first visit to Cuba by a leader from the Caribbean Community (Caricom), the economic alliance of English-speaking Caribbean nations, since the late Jamaican Prime Minister Michael Manley visited more than 15 years ago.
